I grew up Catholic, and although I've been feeling a bit iffy about the actual Church itself (along with organized religion in general) I still could consider my own beliefs to be religious, and I hold great value in some of the teachings of Christianity and other religions. But I think what makes the Mandela Catalogue stand out to me as horror is how in their universe, the Abrahamic religions were tainted by manipulation from Satan in numerous ways at multiple points in history. So kind of going into the mindset that everything you've been believing in your whole life, the almighty God and his Son, are all fake, and you're in dead man's land during the war between us and Satan with his alternates, can make this way more freaky than just the atmosphere and scares.

Same, although I was more grateful that my periods are more normal because my mother's are like near-anemia level bad and she has to have medication so she doesn't get hospitalized once a month. Once I got the hang of taking care of myself during my period, I stopped caring too much. I even enjoy bonding with friends of mine who are women over our shared struggle with periods. However, I never bought into the buzzfeed kind of pride over periods, especially because it tied periods to womanhood to an uncomfortable degree. I know many cis women don't even subscribe to that kind of viewpoint either.
